anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
gauntlet: question
The gathered draft says the existing resolver cannot accept overrides, but primary code shows otherwise. `settings/resolver.ts:11` already accepts a timeout override, and I traced every caller to that same resolver, so it already owns timeout resolution. The missing override comes from the caller not passing its value, not from a gap in the resolver. A second settings file would add a parallel boundary beside the one that already handles this case. No ticket decision settles the point, and the design will proceed on this corrected fact unless you override it.

A) as framed: add a second settings file that supplies the timeout override.
B) pivot: change the existing caller to pass its timeout override to the resolver - `settings/resolver.ts:11` already supports the override, and all callers use it.
C) smaller or none: ship no new settings path and leave the missing override unresolved.
Recommendation: B - it fixes the root cause through the existing boundary without duplicating settings ownership.

gauntlet: question
The draft’s claim that the existing resolver cannot accept overrides is contradicted by `settings/resolver.ts:11`, which already accepts a timeout override. Tracing every caller confirmed that all use this resolver. A second settings file would duplicate that boundary; the root-cause alternative is to change the existing caller to pass its override.

Which direction should the design take?
A) as framed — add a second settings file.
B) pivot: pass the timeout override through the existing caller — the resolver already supports it.
C) smaller or none: leave the behavior unchanged and document the missing override.
Recommendation: B - it fixes the missing override at the existing boundary without creating a parallel settings path.
